detail: Git version control established in this repository on this date. This variant log begins here. It does NOT cover any prior session, change, or decision made before version control existed -- there is no retroactive entry for earlier work. See PROVENANCE.md for the full disclosure of what this means for commit-history-based verification.

description: Repository audit + real commit hashes backfilled after git init
what_was_tried: Wrote docs/AUDIT_A_COLUMN.md classifying 11 previously-claimed capabilities as VERIFIED/PARTIAL against real artefacts; re-ran it once git existed to attach real commit hashes; disclosed the pre-commit hook's own verification (including one accidentally-committed then reflog-pruned test commit) in PROVENANCE.md.
why: Client's stated acceptance rule requires a commit ID plus an inspectable artefact for every claimed capability; this closed that gap honestly rather than silently upgrading unverified claims to verified.

description: D1 feature-block separation refactor: features/ package split out of stage1_step4_vectors.py
what_was_tried: Wrote a byte-exact golden snapshot test (tests/test_refactor_snapshot.py) BEFORE moving any code (G5 safety net), then split the vector formulas/calibration/window/attention code into features/{geometry,x_core,episodes,attention}.py, turned stage1_step4_vectors.py into an orchestrator importing from those modules, updated the other two loop consumers (stage3_demo_ui.py, analyze_video.py), and added machine-checked import/call-graph + runtime-monkeypatch separation tests (tests/test_feature_separation.py) plus docs/D1_DEPENDENCY_MAP.md for outside reviewers.
why: CLAUDE.md's D1 requirement (attention/audio must never reach X_core/E_t) needs to be a structural, block-separated codebase, not just a documented convention -- and G5 requires proving no formula/threshold/behavior changed during the move, not just asserting it.

description: D6 precision simulation built out: synthetic generator, fit/bootstrap CI, sweep grid, PNG->SVG fix
what_was_tried: Built simulation/generator.py (synthetic trial-sequence generator), simulation/models.py + precision.py (fit/evaluate/bootstrap CI on the primary metric Delta), a concrete sweep grid with results/docs (artefacts/precision_analysis_v1.md), then caught and fixed a G4 violation where sweep plots were written as PNG (media-guard blocks *.png) and switched them to SVG.
why: D0PA1's D6 precision-simulation work item (CLAUDE.md 'WHAT D0PA1 ADDS') needed a synthetic-data pipeline to characterize the primary metric's precision before any real data collection; the PNG fix was a real near-miss against G4, caught and corrected the same session rather than left in place.

description: D6 generator gains rare classes (ABANDON/NO_ACTION); D0PA1 null-input + negative controls built; Pass 2 sweep
what_was_tried: Extended the synthetic generator to support n_classes=5 including rare ABANDON/NO_ACTION outcomes; built controls/null_input.py (real-webcam null-input control, MAD+std dispersion measurement) and controls/negative_control.py; added refit-per-replicate bootstrap wired through compute_delta; ran a second sweep pass (refit bootstrap x n_classes x session length) and corrected the precision-analysis CI writeup (v2) to match.
why: A single-class, single-bootstrap-style sweep understated real precision uncertainty and didn't cover the rare-outcome case the real study will actually see (ABANDON/NO_ACTION as real classes, not absent rows -- see CLAUDE.md D0PA1 hard constraints); the controls give a real (not simulated) measurement of sensor/pipeline noise before any threshold is signed.

description: D6 finalisation pass: joint grid at n_boot=200, Monte Carlo spread
what_was_tried: Ran a finalisation sweep at a higher bootstrap replicate count (n_boot=200) across a joint parameter grid, documented the code-level account in D6_SIMULATION.md section 10, and added a finalisation addendum to precision_analysis_v2.md covering the joint grid and worst-cell result.
why: Earlier sweep passes used a lower bootstrap count for speed during iteration; the finalisation pass exists specifically to check whether the earlier, cheaper sweeps' conclusions hold at a Monte-Carlo-stable replicate count before treating any of it as a settled precision estimate.

description: Primary-metric comparison: log loss vs macro-F1, oriented utility, selectable metric
what_was_tried: Refactored simulation/precision.py to a metric abstraction (macro-F1 or log loss selectable, not hardcoded to one), added an oriented utility function for log loss, built a comparison driver measuring decidability under both metrics, and documented the code-level account (D6_SIMULATION.md section 11) plus the comparison result (precision_analysis_v2.md Addendum 2).
why: The choice of primary metric materially changes what the precision simulation can detect (a metric-selection decision, not just an implementation detail) -- CLAUDE.md G2 requires this kind of choice be examined and fixed in advance, not picked implicitly by whichever metric the code happened to compute first.

description: Log-loss clip epsilon made a pre-registered, hashed parameter (simulation/config.py's origin)
what_was_tried: Found that the log-loss clip epsilon swings the primary metric U by more than 2x between eps=1e-6 and eps=1e-15 on a single exact-zero-probability trial (a real, not pathological, sensitivity); measured that sensitivity on real fitted output (not just the constructed worst case); created simulation/config.py's PreRegisteredConfig specifically to give this one parameter a versioned, hashed home instead of a bare literal; documented both in D6_SIMULATION.md section 12 and precision_analysis_v2.md Addendum 3.
why: A parameter whose value swings a primary metric by 2x is exactly the kind of decision G2 requires be fixed in advance, visibly and verifiably, before it could be tuned after seeing a result -- this is the seed that Gate 0's later A2 generalisation (this same session) grew out of.

description: Feature-separation compatibility-shim blind spot closed; real log evidence produced for the client
what_was_tried: Found that tests/test_feature_separation.py's checks 1-3 only walk the features.* package graph, so an import of stage1_step4_vectors.py (which re-exports attention/audio symbols alongside core ones for historical diagnostic scripts) by x_core.py/episodes.py would launder a forbidden-block reference past every existing check; added check 4 (discovers cross-block shims by AST, not a hardcoded filename) and proved it fails on a real injected violation before reverting. Separately, inspected a real session log end-to-end to answer the client's per-frame-vs-aggregate question with real counts/cadence rather than from memory, and produced docs/LOG_EVIDENCE.md plus a truncated excerpt for emailing.
why: A separation guard that has never been observed to fail is not a guard (same standard the pre-commit media-guard hook was already held to); the log-evidence task was the client asking for real emitted-record evidence specifically because a description of the code is not the same claim as an inspected log.
